title: Top 275 PDF: Words 101 to 125
subtitle: Bibulous to Verisimilitude (SSC CGL 2026 Digital Notes)

words.meaning: Excessively fond of drinking alcohol; highly absorbent like a sponge.
words.example: The bibulous paper quickly soaked up all the spilled ink.

words.meaning: Insolent or insulting language or treatment.
words.example: He bore the contumely of his political opponents with quiet dignity.

words.meaning: Relating to or dependent on charity or the giving of alms.
words.example: The hospital is maintained through eleemosynary contributions.

words.meaning: Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous.
words.example: His equivocal reply left everyone in the committee confused.

words.meaning: Very small in size or amount; meager.
words.example: They struggled to survive on their exiguous monthly income.

words.meaning: Artificially created or developed; not genuine.
words.example: The controversy appeared to be a factitious dispute manufactured by the media.

words.meaning: Difficult to deal with; contrary and stubborn.
words.example: The froward child refused to sit quietly during the lecture.

words.meaning: Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.
words.example: The garrulous old clerk kept talking long after office hours.

words.meaning: Denoting a period of time in the past that was idyllically happy and peaceful.
words.example: He recalled the halcyon days of his college life.

words.meaning: Likely to arouse or incur resentment or anger in others; offensive.
words.example: Making comparisons between siblings is always an invidious task.

words.meaning: Soften or break down by soaking in liquid; make thin or emaciated.
words.example: Long illness had macerated the patient severely.

words.meaning: Wicked, villainous, or criminal in nature.
words.example: The gang was arrested for their nefarious activities.

words.meaning: Expressing scorn or criticism; abusive and shameful.
words.example: The crowd shouted opprobrious remarks at the referee.

words.meaning: Travel or wander around from place to place.
words.example: He spent two years peregrinating across remote villages.

words.meaning: Petty, worthless, or of little value.
words.example: Do not waste your exam prep time on picayune details.

words.meaning: The state of being close to someone or something; proximity.
words.example: The school's propinquity to his home made walking easy.

words.meaning: Cowardly or unfaithful to duty; traitorous.
words.example: The recreant soldier fled the battlefield at first sight of the enemy.

words.meaning: A disposition to laughter; comicality.
words.example: The clown's silly antics appealed to the children's risibility.

words.meaning: Having or conveying undue or inappropriate interest in sexual matters.
words.example: Tabloids rely on salacious gossip to attract readers.

words.meaning: Showing dedication and diligence.
words.example: Through sedulous practice, she mastered the English vocabulary.

words.meaning: Loud and powerful voice or sound.
words.example: The sergeant gave orders in a stentorian tone.

words.meaning: Excessive confidence or boldness; audacity.
words.example: He had the temerity to challenge the director's decision.

words.meaning: Mentally or physically inactive; lethargic.
words.example: Cold weather made the reptiles completely torpid.

words.meaning: Offense or annoyance taken at something said or done.
words.example: He took umbrage at the suggestion that he was cheating.

words.hindi: सच जैसा आभास / वास्तविकता का रूप
words.meaning: The appearance of being true or real.
words.example: The historical novel gives great verisimilitude to period details.
